title: Branches are movable pointers
explanation:
A branch in Git is just a lightweight, movable **pointer** to a commit. When you commit on a branch, that branch's pointer moves forward to the new commit. A special pointer, **HEAD**, tells Git which branch you are currently on.

```bash
git branch experiment        # create a pointer at the current commit; you stay where you are
git switch experiment        # move HEAD to that branch
git switch -c hotfix         # create a branch and switch to it in one step (older: git checkout -b hotfix)
git switch -                 # go back to the previously checked-out branch
```

Switching branches changes your working directory to match the last commit on that branch — Git adds, removes, and modifies files for you. If Git can't do that cleanly — for example because uncommitted edits would be overwritten — it won't let you switch at all, so commit (or otherwise put aside) your work before switching.
keyIdeas: A branch is a lightweight pointer to a commit; it moves when you commit.
HEAD points at the branch you are on.
`git branch name` creates; `git switch name` moves; `git switch -c name` does both.
Switching rewrites your working directory to that branch's last commit.

workedExample.problem: On branch `trunk`, create a branch `specials` *without* leaving `trunk`, then switch to it, commit a new file `specials.md`, and switch back. Show that the file exists only on `specials`.
steps: `git branch specials` creates the pointer at the current commit; `git branch --show-current` still says `trunk`.
`git switch specials` moves HEAD; the commit you make now advances only `specials`.
Switching back with `git switch trunk` makes the working directory match trunk's last commit, so `specials.md` disappears from disk (it is safe in the other branch).

Run it in a throwaway folder:
```sh
git init -q -b trunk shop && cd shop
printf 'tea\n' > menu.md && git add menu.md && git commit -q -m 'Add menu'
git branch specials
[ "$(git branch --show-current)" = trunk ]   # created, but we did not move
git switch -q specials
printf 'iced tea\n' > specials.md && git add specials.md && git commit -q -m 'Add specials'
git switch -q trunk
[ ! -e specials.md ]                           # not on trunk
git ls-tree --name-only specials | grep -qx specials.md
echo ok
```
workedExample.answer: `specials.md` is committed on `specials` only; on `trunk` the file is absent from the working directory, and `trunk` still points at `Add menu`.

pitfalls: Assuming `git branch name` also switches to it — it only creates the pointer.
Switching with uncommitted conflicting edits and being surprised when Git refuses.
Committing on the wrong branch because you didn't check `git status` (it prints the current branch).

citations.quote: A branch in Git is simply a lightweight movable pointer to one of these commits.
This creates a new pointer to the same commit you're currently on.
How does Git know what branch you're currently on? It keeps a special pointer called HEAD.
Create a new branch and switch to it: git switch -c new-branch.
Return to your previously checked out branch: git switch -.
HEAD is the pointer to the current branch reference, which is in turn a pointer to the last commit made on that branch.
If you switch to an older branch, your working directory will be reverted to look like it did the last time you committed on that branch.
If Git cannot do it cleanly, it will not let you switch at all.
